meta.title: The Reference You Already Own
meta.summary: Ionian is the major scale you already play with both of this chapter's dials at their plain setting, and having no characteristic note is exactly what makes it the mode everything else here gets heard against.

It has no characteristic note. No chip lights amber on its scale card, no dot gets outlined in its windows on the neck. That isn't a gap — a characteristic note is whatever separates a scale from its nearest plain relative, and Ionian is the plain relative, the thing every other mode in this pathway gets measured against.
Play it against the drone. One card, and nothing on it lights up — that absence is half of this lesson, heard rather than read.

None of this is jazz-only material, whatever you've heard. Writers on rock harmony broadly agree that Ionian, Mixolydian, Dorian and Aeolian are the common modes of the repertoire, with Phrygian turning up in metal — Everett and Moore among them, and it is a settled reading of the music rather than a measurement,

. Two of those four are in this chapter — Ionian and Mixolydian — and the other two belong to chapter 4. Lydian isn't on the list at all, which is part of why it needs a lesson of its own rather than a mention.

sitting inside it is precisely the note the next mode down the ladder gives up. Naming the chord here is fair game; what you'd do with a seventh chord beyond naming it is a different topic.

For a scale everyone calls the safe one, there is exactly one note in it that fights the chord underneath when you land on it and hold. It has a name, a reason, and an exact place in the scale — all of which is what
The Note That Fights the Chord

Temperley and Tan also derive a scale-degree distribution from de Clercq and Temperley's harmonic analyses of the 200-song rock_corpus dataset, and note that the seven major-scale degrees occur more often than any others — which suggests Ionian predominates specifically. That's an inference from how often individual degrees turn up, not a count of how many songs use each mode.
